themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints exploded to 3 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2,300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting rapid proliferation of unlicensed or noncompliant food operations in Washington Heights/Inwood this week.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Aligns with community board repeated requests for food assistance and public health oversight
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed vendors flooding street corners? Interview DOHMH and local residents about food safety concerns.
Is this linked to summer foot traffic or a new vendor encampment? Map complaint locations.

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Peak
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (likely Uber/Lyft) spiked to 23 complaints 2 weeks ago, up 1,050% from an 8-week average of 2.0 per week (z-score: 12.66)—the highest statistical severity recorded in the dataset—indicating acute traffic, congestion, or safety issues tied to ride-sharing.
evidence: 23 for-hire vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,050% spike)
Z-score of 12.66—highest statistical severity in entire dataset
Suggests concentrated incident or pattern (e.g., illegal pickups, blocking streets, accidents)
reporting_angles: What triggered the spike 2 weeks ago? Was there a concert, event, or service disruption?
Interview residents about traffic gridlock; request TLC data on complaint types and neighborhoods.

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 21 last week, a 380% spike from a 4.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.64), concentrated in a single week—indicating rapid deterioration or newly visible damage across Washington Heights/Inwood pedestrian infrastructure.
evidence: 21 sidewalk condition complaints last week vs. 4.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (380% spike)
Z-score of 7.64 indicates strong statistical anomaly
Convergence: community board has repeatedly requested street/park reconstruction funding (unmet demand)
reporting_angles: Map the 21 complaints—are they clustered on a few blocks or spread citywide? Walkable investigation.
Did heavy rain or recent construction cause sudden deterioration? Interview DOT about repair backlogs.

themes_detail.label: Water System Failures Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints (leaks, pressure issues, outages) surged to 36 last week versus a baseline of 12.8 per week (182% spike, z-score: 5.97), following the broader heat/hot water crisis affecting the district and suggesting infrastructure strain.
evidence: 36 water system complaints last week vs. 12.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (182% spike)
Context: 7,203 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days (highest category) suggests systemic water/heating infrastructure crisis
reporting_angles: Are aging water mains failing during peak summer demand? Request DEP data on breaks and repair priorities.
Is this tied to the broader heat crisis? Profile a building with compounded water + heat complaints.

themes_detail.label: Food Establishment Health Violations
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints jumped to 12 last week, a 231% spike from a 3.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.07)—paired with the 2,300% mobile vendor spike THIS WEEK—indicating a potential food safety crisis across the district's food supply chain.
evidence: 12 food establishment complaints last week vs. 3.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (231% spike)
Z-score of 4.07 indicates strong statistical signal
Convergence: paired with mobile food vendor spike THIS WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.1 baseline)—suggests broader food safety degradation
reporting_angles: Are restaurants losing refrigeration due to heat/power issues? Cross-check against utility outage reports.
Interview DOHMH: Are violations clustered by type (temperature, cleanliness, pest activity)? Any recent enforcement gaps?
